elements.content: Communication Goal: I can put daily actions in order and describe my pace of life.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 4. Daily routine
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Temperament matters
- Materials: Sequence cards, sentence strips, schedule template, COSYmanuals 'sequence words' and 'adverbs of frequency' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use sequence words (first, then, after that, finally)
• describe lifestyle pace and habits
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles daily routine and frequency adverbs from Lessons 13–15.

Next lesson: Lesson 17 moves to weather and impersonal 'it'.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

first — before all the others. Example: First, I wake up.
then — after that. Example: Then, I have breakfast.
after that — next in order. Example: After that, I go to work.
finally — at the end. Example: Finally, I go to bed.
schedule — a plan of times and activities. Example: My schedule is very busy.
busy — having a lot to do. Example: She is busy today.
early — before the usual time. Example: I wake up early.
late — after the usual time. Example: He goes to bed late.
routine — things you do regularly. Example: My daily routine starts at six.
habit — something you do regularly. Example: Reading is a good habit.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• First, I wake up early. (starting a sequence)
• Then, I check my schedule. (continuing a sequence)
• After that, I work. (continuing a sequence)
• Finally, I relax. (ending a sequence)
• My schedule is busy. (describing pace)
• I am usually early. (describing a habit)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'before all the others'?
Which word means 'after that'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Sequence-word stress and linking

first /fɜːst/ — one syllable
then /ðen/ — voiced th
finally /ˈfaɪnəli/ — three syllables
schedule /ˈʃedjuːl/ — stress the first syllable

First, I wake up early. Then, I check my schedule. Finally, I relax.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use sequence words to put actions in order and tell a simple story or routine.

Form:
Sequence words: First, ... Then, ... After that, ... Finally, ... Use a comma after the sequence word at the start of a sentence.

Examples:
• First, I wake up. Then, I have breakfast.
• After that, I go to work.
• Finally, I go home and relax.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
___, I wake up. (step 1)
___, I have breakfast. (step 2)
___, I go to bed. (last step)
___, I go to work. (step 3)
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• First, I ... Then, I ... After that, I ... Finally, I ...
• First, she ... Then, she ... Finally, she ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What do you do first in the morning?
• What do you do after that?
• What do you do finally before bed?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write four sentences about your morning with sequence words.
• Write four sentences about your evening with sequence words.
Reading: Temperament matters

First, I wake up early. Then, I check my busy schedule. After that, I work and study. Finally, I relax at home. My routine is busy, but I like it. My sister has a different temperament. She is usually late, and her schedule is relaxed. We are different, but we are a happy family.
What does the writer do first?
Is the sister usually early or late?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What do you do first in the morning?
B: First, I wake up early. Then, I check my schedule.
A: And after that?
B: After that, I work. Finally, I relax at home.
A: Is your schedule busy?
B: Yes, it is. But I like my routine.
What does the speaker do first?
How is the schedule?
Speaking task: Explain your morning and evening routine to your partner using four sequence words.

• Are you usually early or late?
• Is your schedule busy?
• What do you do first in the morning?
• What do you do finally before bed?
• Do you prefer a busy or a relaxed routine?
Role-play: You are a time-management coach. Ask a client about their routine and suggest one change.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about your routine with sequence words.
Model: First, ... Then, ... After that, ... Finally, ...
